The main tasks were scoped out as: 1. AFP simulation: The simulation will generate tool path planning for two different tank laminate configurations, filament winding (FW) type and ply-by-ply type. The FW will produce the tank wall laminate close to a fabric architecture while the ply-by-ply layup will produce a unidirectional laminate structure. Once the simulation is done, the team planned to review their manufacturing feasibility and limitations. In combination with the tank material evaluation from UDRI, the team would have decided the final laminate structure for tank prototyping. The simulation would also provide inputs on tank boss opening size and shape, and AFP slit tape width. 2. Tooling for inner and outer tanks: Both water soluble mandrel and permanent tool were in consideration for the tank prototype. Page 18 of 30 Approved for Public Release 3. Process development trials for inner and outer tank: The trials were planned to confirm a few key composite manufacturing aspects prior to tank prototyping, including tape steering and defects, tank cure and tool removal. Sealing area tank surface finish (e.g., boss and two halves of outer tank), fiber waviness and voids content are critical to tank performance. 4. AFP fabrication for inner and outer tanks: The tanks were to be fabricated and inspected with x-ray CT. RTRC had estimated the carbon fiber thermoset prepreg tape needs based on the Phase 1 tank prototype work scope. Renegade Materials Corporation was selected as the AFP prepreg tape manufacturer. A PO was placed but later cancelled due to program termination by DOE. 5. Testing of tank (Phase 1 and Phase 2): HYPER lab at WSU was down-selected after getting preliminary quotes from a total of 3 labs. Two tests were planned under Task 7: (i) LH2 boil-off test at an operating pressure of 6 bar, and (ii) burst pressure test, with water at least 13.5 bar (6 bar x 2.25 FoS). The overall test protocol was discussed with WSU and the outlines determined. Additional discussions took place to perform permeability testing of composites, without and with Carbon Nanotubes. The specimens were shipped to Hyper Lab for testing, but were returned due to termination of the program. A test rig for vacuum, with cryogenic capability was being developed at RTRC. The work started but was stopped due to program termination. 6. Risk Assessment and Mitigation approaches: A risk assessment of the LH2 tank was performed and the main risk areas were identified and ranked. The main risk items are shown in Table 2 below. The degree of risk for each item is assessed on a scale from 1 through 5, with 5 being the highest, and 1 being the lowest. Primarily, the risk items are about achieving air-tight sealing and high-quality thermal insulation.
